text: Name a famous AI or ML researcher
note: Surname is enough. Pioneers, deep learning, RL, NLP, vision, theory, robotics, safety and AI lab leaders all count

answers.q: Ran away from home at 15, co-invented the artificial neuron with McCulloch in 1943, never took a degree.
Nobel in economics, Turing Award, and the Logic Theorist. Predicted a chess champion machine within ten years, in 1957.
Popularized 'machine learning' in 1959 with a checkers program that beat him.
Founded cybernetics. Reportedly once forgot whether he'd already had lunch by checking which way he was walking.
ADALINE and the LMS rule with his student Ted Hoff, who went on to co-design the first microprocessor.
Co-wrote Perceptrons, created Logo and the turtle, and once assigned computer vision as a summer project.
Wrote SHRDLU, then became AI's critic, then advised a grad student named Larry Page.
Subsumption architecture, iRobot co-founder, author of 'Elephants Don't Play Chess'.
First author of the 1986 Nature backprop paper. The top cognitive science prize is named after him.
Described backprop for neural nets in his 1974 thesis. Few noticed for a decade.
Neocognitron, 1980. Also an early user of ReLU-like units, back in 1969.
Diagnosed vanishing gradients in his 1991 diploma thesis, then co-invented LSTM. Now xLSTM.
CTC, Neural Turing Machines, handwriting generation. LSTMs that write cursive.
Made SGD respectable. Co-wrote Lush and DjVu along the way.
Random forests, bagging, and 'Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures'.
Invented the lasso in 1996. Also co-wrote ESL and ISLR.
Berkeley's ML patriarch. Not the basketball one, though IEEE once called him that.
Stanley's team lead, Google X and self-driving founder, Udacity co-founder.
Sutton's PhD adviser and co-author. Shared the 2024 Turing Award.
Kernel methods, then causality. Co-founded the Tübingen ELLIS hub.
First author of both Adam and the VAE. Two of the most-cited papers in ML.
Information theory, Bayesian neural nets and 'Sustainable Energy Without the Hot Air'.
LDA, 2003. Topic models for everything, for a decade.
t-SNE, with Hinton, 2008.
XGBoost, then TVM and MXNet. Kaggle owes him a statue.
Co-created PyTorch.
Created Keras and the ARC benchmark. Skeptical of LLM hype in 280-character increments.
AlexNet, trained on two GTX 580s in his bedroom.
GoogLeNet, and first to show adversarial examples, in 2013.
YOLO's creator, whose CV resume had My Little Pony on it. Quit vision research over military use.
SIFT, 1999. Patented, so OpenCV kept it in a contrib module for years.
StyleGAN. The faces on 'This Person Does Not Exist' are his.
The attention mechanism, 2014, before it was all you needed.
Transformer co-author, mixture-of-experts, Character.AI. Google paid billions to rehire him.
Youngest Transformer author, an intern at the time. Co-founded Cohere.
First author of GPT, GPT-2, CLIP, Whisper and DCGAN. Rarely tweets.
Physicist who wrote the 2020 scaling-laws paper, then co-founded Anthropic.
Coined 'stochastic parrots' with Gebru et al. Also the #BenderRule: name your language.
First author of the chain-of-thought prompting paper.
FlashAttention. Made attention IO-aware and everyone's GPUs faster.
Mamba and S4. State-space models' main advocate.
Mechanistic interpretability pioneer, no undergrad degree, Distill co-founder.
Co-invented RLHF, then founded the Alignment Research Center.
TRPO, PPO, and an OpenAI co-founder.
DeepMind co-founder who popularized the term 'AGI'.
First author of DQN, the Atari paper that started deep RL.
WaveNet, PixelCNN, VQ-VAE, CPC. A one-man generative model factory.
Seq2seq, the Google 'cat neuron', and neural architecture search.
Libratus and Pluribus beat poker pros. Now at OpenAI working on reasoning.
Introduced diffusion models in 2015, five years before they took over.
Led AlphaFold 2. Shared the 2024 chemistry Nobel with Hassabis and David Baker.
Self-taught alignment researcher, LessWrong founder, wrote a Harry Potter fanfic about rationality.
Wrote GEB. Spent decades on analogy, then got worried about LLMs.
DeepSeek's founder, who funded it from his quant hedge fund.
PAC learning, 1984. Turing Award 2010.
DeepMind co-founder, former chess prodigy and game designer, 2024 chemistry Nobel for AlphaFold.
Built ImageNet when most thought datasets were boring. Then co-founded World Labs.
Invented GANs in 2014, reportedly after an argument at a Montreal bar.
TD learning, the RL textbook, The Bitter Lesson, and a 2024 Turing Award with Barto.
Coined 'artificial intelligence' for the 1956 Dartmouth proposal and invented Lisp.
Co-founded MIT's AI Lab. His Perceptrons book is blamed for chilling neural nets.
Information theory, a juggling machine, a maze-solving mouse, and Dartmouth co-organizer.
Built the Mark I Perceptron in 1958. Died in a boating accident in 1971, before the revival.
Hopfield networks, 1982. Shared the 2024 physics Nobel with Hinton.
Bayesian networks, do-calculus, The Book of Why. Turing Award 2011.
VC theory with Chervonenkis, then SVMs. Moved from Moscow to Bell Labs in 1990.
Google's chief scientist. Compilers don't warn him; he warns compilers.
ResNet, Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN, MAE. The most-cited paper of the century, by some counts.
First author of 'Attention Is All You Need'.
word2vec, 2013. Also showed that king − man + woman ≈ queen.
OpenAI CEO. Fired and rehired within five days in November 2023.
Left OpenAI to co-found Anthropic in 2021. Wrote 'Machines of Loving Grace'.
Led AlphaGo, AlphaZero and the RL lectures everyone watches.
LSTM co-inventor. Also co-invented, he would like you to know, most of the rest.
AlexNet co-author, seq2seq, OpenAI co-founder, then Safe Superintelligence. Feels the AGI.
Backprop popularizer, Boltzmann machine co-inventor, 2024 physics Nobel. Left Google in 2023 to warn about AI.
Convnets in 1989, bank cheques in the '90s, Turing Award 2018, and a very active poster.
The most-cited computer scientist alive, by most counts. Turing Award 2018.
Coursera co-founder, Google Brain co-founder, Baidu's chief scientist. Taught millions gradient descent.
Coined 'Software 2.0' and 'vibe coding'. Ran Tesla Autopilot's vision team. Now teaches via YouTube.
Asked 'Can machines think?' in 1950, then swapped it for a party game.
